sections.heading: Keeping right, right of way and emergency vehicles
sections.markdown:
## C — Keeping right, right of way and emergency vehicles

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A56
Traffic moving below the normal speed for the time, location and conditions should use the available right lane or stay as far right as practicable. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A56
The keep-right rule allows overtaking same-direction traffic and preparing for a left turn at an intersection, private road or driveway. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A56
At an uncontrolled intersection, vehicles arriving at about the same time yield to traffic on their right. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A56
Drive defensively even when you appear entitled to proceed, because another driver might not stop. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A56
Before reaching a yield-controlled intersection, look for crossing traffic. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A56
Yield to crossing traffic close enough to create a conflict, including when turning onto a road. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A56
After finding a safe traffic gap, merge and adjust travelling speed. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A56
A driver approaching the stop-controlled side of a two-way-stop intersection must stop fully before entering. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A57
At a two-way stop, look in every direction and wait for conflicting vehicles and pedestrians to clear before proceeding. [A57] [A56]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A57
At a four-way stop, every driver must stop and exercise ordinary care while crossing. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A57
First-stop-first-go is described as common courtesy at a four-way stop; when uncertain, yield to the driver on the right. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A57
Do not insist on priority if doing so risks a crash. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A57
Roundabout traffic circulates one way counterclockwise around the central island. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A57
A roundabout's truck apron provides turning room for the rear wheels of large trucks. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A57
Cars, SUVs, pickups, cyclists and pedestrians may not use the truck apron. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A57
Approach a roundabout at the posted advisory speed and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in the approach crosswalk. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A57
Yield to vehicles approaching from the left that are already circulating, and enter only a safe gap. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A57
Signal right when nearing your roundabout exit and yield to pedestrians and cyclists in the exit crosswalk. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A57
Before entering a two-lane roundabout, use its signs and arrows to select the correct lane. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A57
In the described general two-lane layout, left turns use the shared through/left lane and right turns use the shared through/right lane. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A57
For straight travel through a two-lane roundabout, follow its signs and arrows, yield to all circulating traffic on the left and remain in the selected lane. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A57
Avoid driving beside or passing a large truck at a roundabout because it may need another lane or the apron to turn. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A57
For an emergency vehicle, pull over before entering a roundabout; if already inside, take your exit and pull over beyond the splitter island. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A57
Avoid stopping inside the roundabout while yielding to an emergency vehicle. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

Misconceptions: An apparent right of way never justifies forcing a collision; moving around a roundabout and pulling over before entering are different emergency responses.
Mnemonics: See the conflict, yield the space, enter only a safe gap.
Glossary: A truck apron is the raised paved area for large vehicles' rear wheels; a splitter island separates entering and leaving roundabout traffic.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.
